notes: ὁ λεγόμενος is appositional to the anarthrous Σίμων rather than governing an expressed head noun, so rule 90 and not rule 31 applies and the article takes who while the participle keeps is called. Reading Σίμων as the article's expressed head noun, which would empty the article under rule 31 and give who is called to the participle, remains defensible.

The son of Zebedee follows rule 57's after-the-head configuration: the outer article takes the determiner plus the supplied nominal under rule 102, and the inner article, having no determiner to anchor, is unrepresented under rule 23 with of riding on the name.
